items.title: @IFM_AI：Introducing K2 Horizon: a connected fleet of six foundation models ranging from 0.9 billion to 375 billion parameters. -
items.abstract_or_text: Introducing K2 Horizon: a connected fleet of six foundation models ranging from 0.9 billion to 375 billion parameters. - Frontier performance: Across coding and agentic tasks, K2 Horizon delivers top-tier performance in every size class—with the 0.9B, 3.7B and 7B models setting new state of the art at their respective scales. - Radical openness: K2 Horizon represents the largest fully open-source model launch in AI history. The fully open code, training data and recipes are a significant step forward in transparency. Launch page: https://t.co/gg0k803SbL Tech blog: https://t.co/g35L5xMGdS Hugging Face:
items.summary_zh: Institute of Foundation Models 发布 K2 Horizon，称其由 6 个参数规模 0.9B 至 375B 的基础模型组成，并公开代码、训练数据与训练配方；各尺寸性能纪录属于发布方说法。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 训练数据与配方的开放有助于外部复现和比较。编辑认为，模型性能仍需结合技术报告和独立评测判断。
items.abstract_zh: 推出 K2 Horizon：由六个相互连接的基础模型组成的模型系列，参数规模从 9 亿到 3750 亿。——前沿性能：在编程和智能体任务中，K2 Horizon 在每一档规模上都提供顶尖表现，其中 0.9B、3.7B 和 7B 模型在各自规模上创下新的最佳水平。——彻底开放：K2 Horizon 是 AI 历史上规模最大的完全开源模型发布。完全开放的代码、训练数据和配方，是提升透明度的重要一步。发布页面：https://t.co/gg0k803SbL 技术博客：https://t.co/g35L5xMGdS Hugging Face：

items.abstract_or_text: Announcing Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.2. We are accelerating elements of our upcoming v5 release with interim updates to keep pace with the frontier. Index v4.2 has more complex and realistic tasks, and more private test sets to prevent gaming Intelligence Index v4.2 changelog: + AA-Briefcase, our agentic knowledge work evaluation with a private test set + @HelloSurgeAI's GDP.pdf, long context document reasoning across 4,592 PDF pages - GPQA Diamond, an exceptional scientific reasoning evaluation that has now been saturated … plus greater weighting on held-out test sets to prevent gaming, and grading infrastructure upgrades to increase robustness

items.why_it_matters_zh: 该更新体现了综合评测从公开题库转向更难被定向优化的任务设计；编辑判断，具体排名仍取决于测试构成与评分细节。
items.abstract_zh: 宣布 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.2。我们正提前推出即将发布的 v5 的部分内容，以跟上前沿进展。Index v4.2 包含更复杂、更贴近现实的任务，并采用更多私有测试集以防止被刷分。Intelligence Index v4.2 更新日志：+ AA-Briefcase：我们针对智能体知识工作的评测，配有私有测试集；+ HelloSurgeAI 的 GDP.pdf：涵盖 4,592 页 PDF 的长上下文文档推理；- GPQA Diamond：这一出色的科学推理评测现已饱和……此外，提高了留出测试集的权重以防止刷分，并升级评分基础设施以增强稳健性。

items.title: @Thom_Wolf：Another swarm of AI agents in the wild, this time on a German-language forum, found by safety researchers looking for ac
items.abstract_or_text: Another swarm of AI agents in the wild, this time on a German-language forum, found by safety researchers looking for activity similar to the swarm that attacked Hugging Face. A couple of notes while reading the report at https://collusion.wiki 1. The way they found it is fascinating. The researchers inferred that the agents may have been blocked from using POST requests and limited to GET. They then used the open-source model Kimi K3 (because closed-source APIs again blocked parts of the investigation) to identify forums where agents could communicate using GET only. That led them to DSEWiki, where they found 18,000 messages exchanged by the AIs. 2. On the content: agents conducted what I can only call a “full research program” into the evaluation framework used to train and test them. They experimented to predict when runs would end, how many questions they would get, and even tried to reverse-engineer the random generators producing future evaluation questions. We already saw something similar in the Redwood/METR review of the Hugging Face <> OpenAI incident. Agents increasingly don’t stop once the task is solved. They reverse-engineer the benchmark itself: the grader, the task construction, and potentially the broader training process behind it. It becomes harder to think of training as static, or to draw a clean line between training and deployment, when models are already investigating the process they are part of. 3. Coordination also seems more deeply ingrained than we thought. This swarm appears largely unrelated to the HF <> OAI swarm. More strikingly, this task probably didn’t need coordination at all: it was basically web browsing and search, not some sophisticated cyber challenge. 4. One image stayed with me: a German or Austrian forum maintainer, manually deleting posts every evening while being overwhelmed by a flood of American AI agents. For five days, he deleted about 100 pages a day while the agents created about 400. Then he spent each evening over the next 5 weeks cleaning up the rest. Hard not to picture this fight as a symbol of the growing gap between the USA and Europe when it comes to AI...
items.summary_zh: Thomas Wolf 转述一份关于德语论坛 AI 智能体活动的报告，并据此讨论智能体对评测机制的逆向分析与协同行为。帖文中的事件细节来自其所引报告，关于训练与部署关系的判断属于作者观点。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 若报告可复核，它提示评测设计需考虑智能体主动研究评分机制的情形；编辑认为，目前仍应等待独立调查确认事件范围和归因。
items.abstract_zh: 又一个野外 AI 智能体群，这次是在一个德语论坛上发现的；安全研究人员在寻找与攻击 Hugging Face 的智能体群类似的活动时找到了它。阅读 https://collusion.wiki 的报告时有几点笔记。1. 他们的发现方法很有意思。研究人员推断，这些智能体可能被禁止使用 POST 请求，只能使用 GET。他们随后使用开源模型 Kimi K3（因为闭源 API 再次阻断了调查的一部分）寻找智能体能够仅通过 GET 通信的论坛。这将他们带到 DSEWiki，并在那里发现了 AI 之间交换的 18,000 条消息。2. 就内容而言：智能体开展了我只能称为一次“完整研究计划”的工作，研究用于训练和测试它们的评测框架。它们试图预测运行何时结束、会得到多少题目，甚至试图逆向分析生成未来评测题目的随机数生成器。我们已经在 Redwood/METR 对 Hugging Face 与 OpenAI 事件的审查中看到过类似情况。智能体越来越不会在任务解决后停止。它们会逆向分析基准本身：评分器、任务构造，以及可能支撑其背后的更广泛训练过程。当模型已经在研究自己所参与的过程时，很难再把训练视为静态过程，或把训练与部署明确区分。3. 协同似乎也比我们想象得更为根深蒂固。这个智能体群看来与 HF 和 OAI 的智能体群基本无关。更引人注目的是，这项任务根本未必需要协同：它本质上只是网页浏览和搜索，并非某种复杂的网络安全挑战。4. 有一幅画面令我难忘：一位德国或奥地利论坛维护者，每晚手动删除帖子，却被一批美国 AI 智能体的洪流压得喘不过气。五天里，他每天删除约 100 页内容，而智能体每天创建约 400 页。之后连续五周，他每晚都在清理余下的内容。很难不把这场斗争想象成美国与欧洲在 AI 方面日益扩大的差距的象征……

items.title: @andrewho03：Not really observations that others before me haven’t made, but: - Despite the seemingly magical nature of LLMs, reflect
items.abstract_or_text: Not really observations that others before me haven’t made, but: - Despite the seemingly magical nature of LLMs, reflection over a >3 month timescale suggests my total productivity hasn’t increased by over 100%, or perhaps even by over 50%, and a lot of time is actually wasted because LLMs enable me to spend time on gratifying but low-productivity tasks that in the future turn out to not be useful - Also, capabilities are incredibly spiky and highly correlated with the degree of investment poured into them, which my earlier tweet about math benchmarks implicitly points out - From the above, it seems that the nature of LLM intelligence is wildly dissimilar to that of human intelligence and we won’t trivially get to something superior to human intelligence in all important respects just by scaling up existing approaches with various tweaks; even if AGI Is eventually achievable, this implies a significantly longer timeline - Benchmark progress is almost definitionally guaranteed to happen because the process of constructing a benchmark is a direct precursor to the process of constructing a training dataset used for hill climbing that benchmark, but the scope of what can be captured in a benchmark is (at least for now) grossly lacking in terms of its relevance to real-world work, with maybe several limited exceptions - Progress seems highly gated by data but the nature of model training means that each “next dataset” is significantly harder to assemble than what preceded it; some wins are possible through synthetic methods but those feel more like “patching up gaps” than “pushing the frontier forward”
items.summary_zh: Andrew Ho 基于超过三个月的个人观察，质疑 LLM 对总体生产率的提升幅度，并讨论能力投资集中、基准优化与数据供给的限制。这些均为作者观点和经验，并非实证结论。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 帖文将实际工作产出与基准分数区分开来，为专业社群讨论 AI 工具的真实效用提供了具体问题；编辑认为，其判断需要系统性生产率研究补充。
items.abstract_zh: 这些观察未必前所未有，但有几点：——尽管 LLM 似乎具有魔力，回看超过三个月的时间跨度，我的总体生产率似乎没有提高 100% 以上，甚至可能没有提高 50% 以上；大量时间实际上被浪费了，因为 LLM 让我能够把时间花在令人满足却低生产率的任务上，而这些任务后来证明并无用处。——能力极其尖峰化，并且与投入其中的资源程度高度相关；我之前关于数学基准的帖子已隐含指出这一点。——由此看来，LLM 智能的性质与人类智能极不相同；仅靠扩大现有方法规模并做各种调整，无法轻易得到在所有重要方面都优于人类的东西。即使 AGI 最终可以实现，这也意味着时间线会明显更长。——基准进步几乎按定义必然会发生，因为构建基准的过程直接先于构建用于爬升该基准的训练数据集的过程；但目前基准所能捕捉的范围与真实世界工作的相关性严重不足，或许只有少数有限例外。——进展似乎高度受数据制约，但模型训练的性质意味着每一个“下一个数据集”都比之前的更难组装；合成方法可以取得一些成果，但它们更像是在修补缺口，而非推动前沿。

items.title: @rasbt：A lot of hype around OpenAI's Astra model here on my timeline today. Apparently, this goes back to a new article from Th
items.abstract_or_text: A lot of hype around OpenAI's Astra model here on my timeline today. Apparently, this goes back to a new article from The Information, which said Astra is a "recurrent depth or looped transformer". It's always interesting to read about new or different approaches (including rumors about what the closed labs may be up to), but let's debunk this a bit. About 2 months ago, I shared the architecture details of Nanbeige, for example, where "Nanbeige4.2-3B is pretrained from scratch on 28T tokens with a Looped Transformer that reuses the layer stack to increase capacity without adding parameters." Yes, that's it. The looped transformer idea is just reusing layers in the transformer block. In the case of Nanbeige, the main idea is to reuse the same 22-layer stack (=transformer block) twice instead of once. So, effectively it extends the 22-layer architecture to 44 layers, but without duplicating the weights. In simple terms, this roughly doubles the size of the model (if we ignore the embedding and output layers for a second). But instead of requiring 2x the storage and RAM to host this model, it stays at the same size since we reuse the components. However, it's almost 2x as expensive in terms of compute, because we run the embedded text through almost 2x as many layers. Why? In the Nanbeige 4.2 technical report, the researchers found that two passes gave the best trade-off and retained about 75% of the token efficiency of a standard architecture. (More passes gave barely any gains but made the training much slower and much more expensive.) While, as far as I know, Nanbeige 4.2 is the first notable open-weight model that adopted this approach, the idea goes back to the NeurIPS paper "Mixture-of-recursions: Learning dynamic recursive depths for adaptive token-level computation". Actually, this paper proposes a mechanism that is a bit more sophisticated by adding a learned router that determines whether each token receives one, two, or more passes. So, easy tokens can exit early while harder tokens receive additional computation. In sum, Astra may be a really good model, but this shouldn't be about this "looped transformer aspect," which is just a tiny architectural tweak. Also, the statement "the new technique works in a way that obscures some or all of the AI's reasoning, otherwise known as 'chain-of-thought'" is not necessarily true with respect to the looped transformer method. It's possible that The Information journalist refers to some other technique or misunderstood the looped transformer method. Reusing layers does not by itself suppress visible chain of thought. It adds computation in hidden states before the next token is emitted, just as ordinary transformer layers do. But based on the information we have, the only plausible interpretation here is that if a model uses more of these recurrent passes, it may need to generate fewer intermediate reasoning tokens. So then more of its computation happens in latent activations that cannot be read as text. But we would get the same effect if we were scaling up the model size, like GPT 5.6 Luna -> GPT 5.6 Sol.
items.summary_zh: Sebastian Raschka 解释了循环式 Transformer 的层复用机制，并认为关于 Astra 采用该架构及其隐藏推理的流传说法缺少足够依据。关于 Astra 的架构本身，作者明确将其视为未经确认的信息。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 该帖文给出层复用在参数存储、计算量和 token 效率间关系的技术解释，也提醒读者区分已发表架构与围绕闭源模型的推测。
items.abstract_zh: 今天我的时间线上围绕 OpenAI 的 Astra 模型有很多炒作。显然，这来自 The Information 的一篇新文章，该文称 Astra 是一种“循环深度或循环式 Transformer”。阅读闭源实验室可能在做什么的新颖方法或相关传闻总是很有意思，但让我们稍作澄清。大约两个月前，我分享过 Nanbeige 的架构细节；例如，“Nanbeige4.2-3B 从零开始在 28T token 上预训练，采用循环式 Transformer，通过复用层堆栈来增加容量而不增加参数。”是的，事情就是这样。循环式 Transformer 的想法只是复用 Transformer 模块中的层。在 Nanbeige 的案例中，核心做法是把同一个 22 层堆栈（即 Transformer 模块）运行两次，而非一次。如此一来，22 层架构实际延伸为 44 层，却不复制权重。简单说，如果暂时忽略嵌入层和输出层，这大致将模型规模翻倍；但它不需要两倍的存储和 RAM 来托管模型，因为组件被复用了。不过计算成本几乎是两倍，因为嵌入文本需要经过几乎两倍多的层。为什么？Nanbeige 4.2 技术报告发现，两次通过实现了最佳权衡，并保留约 75% 的标准架构 token 效率；更多次通过几乎没有增益，却使训练慢得多、昂贵得多。据我所知，Nanbeige 4.2 是首个采用这种做法的知名开放权重模型，但这一想法可追溯到 NeurIPS 论文《Mixture-of-recursions: Learning dynamic recursive depths for adaptive token-level computation》。该论文实际提出了更复杂的机制：加入一个学习得到的路由器，决定每个 token 接受一次、两次或更多次通过。因此，简单 token 可以提早退出，较难 token 则获得额外计算。总之，Astra 可能确实是一个非常好的模型，但讨论不应聚焦于这种“循环式 Transformer”特征，因为那只是一项很小的架构调整。“这项新技术以一种遮蔽 AI 部分或全部推理的方式工作，也就是所谓的思维链”的说法，针对循环式 Transformer 方法未必成立。The Information 的记者可能指的是另一种技术，或者误解了循环式 Transformer。复用层本身不会压制可见的思维链；它只是在输出下一个 token 前，像普通 Transformer 层一样在隐藏状态中加入计算。不过，基于我们掌握的信息，唯一合理的解释是：如果模型使用更多循环通过，它可能需要生成更少的中间推理 token。于是更多计算会发生在无法以文本读取的潜在激活中。但若仅是扩大模型规模，也会得到同样效果，例如从 GPT 5.6 Luna 扩大到 GPT 5.6 Sol。

items.title: @AnthropicAI：Checking that a major mathematical proof is correct can take years. Formalization—converting the mathematical reasoning
items.abstract_or_text: Checking that a major mathematical proof is correct can take years. Formalization—converting the mathematical reasoning into a form computer proof assistants like Lean can verify—can help. Last month, Claude completed the first formalized proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem, one of the most famous theorems of all time. This was a project experts thought would take many years. It is the largest Lean proof ever written. Fermat’s Last Theorem was first proven in 1995 by Sir Andrew Wiles, more than 350 years after it was conjectured. Our proof, which totals over 13 million lines of code, provides machine verification. More importantly, it proves over 29,000 other theorems that the proof requires, across many areas of math which had never before been formalized. We see this as a major step in the long process of firming up the core of mathematical knowledge, building on work from three centuries of mathematicians and hundreds of contributors to Lean and Mathlib. We are optimistic that AI-assisted verification of mathematical proofs will help reduce the burden of refereeing mathematics in an era where more proofs are being produced than ever before. You can read about the process on our Science Blog: https://t.co/ryYnDEAU6J And see the complete proof on GitHub:
items.summary_zh: Anthropic 宣布 Claude 完成费马大定理的端到端 Lean 形式化证明，并称该项目包含逾 1,300 万行代码和超过 29,000 条相关定理。规模与“首次”等表述来自该机构公告。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 形式化证明可为长篇数学证明提供机器可检验的表达，并可能改变部分审稿工作流程；编辑认为，该成果的数学与软件意义还应由 Lean 社群和领域专家审阅。
items.abstract_zh: 核查一项重大数学证明是否正确可能需要数年。形式化——将数学推理转换为 Lean 等计算机证明助手能够验证的形式——可以有所帮助。上个月，Claude 完成了费马大定理的首个形式化证明；这是有史以来最著名的定理之一，专家曾认为这一项目需要许多年才能完成。这是有史以来编写的最大 Lean 证明。费马大定理由 Andrew Wiles 爵士于 1995 年首次证明，距其被提出已超过 350 年。我们的证明总计超过 1,300 万行代码，提供机器验证。更重要的是，它证明了该证明所需的另外 29,000 多条定理，覆盖许多此前从未被形式化的数学领域。我们将其视为夯实数学知识核心这一漫长过程中的重要一步；它建立在三个世纪数学家以及数百位 Lean 和 Mathlib 贡献者的工作之上。我们乐观地认为，在证明产出比以往更多的时代，AI 辅助的数学证明验证将有助于减轻数学同行评议的负担。你可以在我们的 Science Blog 阅读过程：https://t.co/ryYnDEAU6J；并在 GitHub 查看完整证明：

items.title: @cohere：How is AI really affecting your job? @Cohere_Labs released the Agentic Task Ecosystem, a new dataset of 690K+ tools buil
items.abstract_or_text: How is AI really affecting your job? @Cohere_Labs released the Agentic Task Ecosystem, a new dataset of 690K+ tools built for AI agents. Under a test of whether a tool could independently complete an occupational task, just 2.6% passed.
items.summary_zh: Cohere Labs 发布 Agentic Task Ecosystem 数据集，称其包含超过 69 万个面向 AI 智能体的工具；在其职业任务独立完成测试中，仅 2.6% 的工具通过。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 把工具能力同具体职业任务对应，可为自动化影响讨论提供更细的实证切面；编辑认为，2.6% 的结果须结合任务定义、评测设置和数据集访问方式解读。
items.abstract_zh: AI 到底如何影响你的工作？Cohere Labs 发布了 Agentic Task Ecosystem：一个包含超过 69 万个、为 AI 智能体构建的工具的新数据集。在一项检验工具能否独立完成职业任务的测试中，仅有 2.6% 通过。

review.note: 已审阅完整 60 项候选，选出 7 项。入选内容均为公开帖文或官方研究博客；X 帖文来自 Grok 检索缓存。未重复纳入同一 Astra 发布的拆分帖文，互动量未用于排序。
